analyticalQuestion: How much exact-launch carrier suppression is lost under arbitrary physical phases, and how does that loss change the sufficient coupling-layer region?
takeaway: The coherent equal-modulus family has an M^-10/3 geometric prefactor, whereas an odd-generation Rudin-Shapiro sign family attains the sharp arbitrary-phase order M^-8/3. A fixed positive observation time has an M^-3 tail prefactor.
palettePolicy: hard two-root cap: muted blue and ochre plus neutral references
nonColorEncoding: filled circles, open squares, and open triangles
fixed panel order from prefactor sharpness to sufficient boundaries

panels.A: exact coherent and Rudin-Shapiro geometric prefactors
panels.B: coherent, arbitrary-phase, and fixed-positive-tail sufficient boundaries

claimBoundary: The prefactor sharpness is algebraic and does not prove actual root-ledger saturation. Phase boundaries are sufficient strict regions. Positive burn-in controls only the remaining tail. The figure contains no DNS or general Navier-Stokes endpoint claim.
